entries.key:
That endpoint is undocumented: it is what Claude Code itself calls, it carries no stability
promise, and it may change or disappear at any time. Token Pace then shows no quota figures
rather than guessing any.
entries.why: T17 (1.14): the English's hard wraps — as many lines as the English, each at most 100 characters — re-wrap, and shorten only where the words do not fit

entries.key:
The token is only read, never refreshed, and appears in no log line or error message. The
target address is hard-coded and cannot be configured. Nothing is sent anywhere else, and
no usage data is collected by this extension.
entries.why: T17 (1.14): the English's hard wraps — as many lines as the English, each at most 100 characters — re-wrap, and shorten only where the words do not fit

entries.key:
Each of them is the documented exchange format (schema_version 1) other tools read, so a
panel, a shell prompt and this extension can share one fetch instead of three.
entries.why: T17 (1.14): the English's hard wraps — as many lines as the English, each at most 100 characters — re-wrap, and shorten only where the words do not fit

entries.key:
They contain the provider's quota response — percentages, reset times, plan type. They
never contain your access token. An existing file whose fetch time is newer than ours is
never overwritten, and the write is atomic (temp file plus rename), so a reader never
sees half a file.
entries.why: T17 (1.14): the English's hard wraps — as many lines as the English, each at most 100 characters — re-wrap, and shorten only where the words do not fit

entries.key:
To read quota figures without any network access, it can register a small script as Claude
Code's status line. Claude Code then runs that script on every status-line refresh and pipes
its status JSON into it; the script keeps of it only the fields Token Pace reads — the quota
windows, the plan, the context window, the cost, the model, the prompt cache and the session's
id — in a file, and prints a status line. The session's name, its working directory, its
transcript's path and the rest of the JSON never reach the file.
entries.why: T17 (1.14): the English's hard wraps — as many lines as the English, each at most 100 characters — re-wrap, and shorten only where the words do not fit

entries.key:
An existing status-line command is kept: it is called by the script with the same input and
its output is passed through unchanged. A settings.json that cannot be parsed is never
touched. The script never sends anything anywhere and never logs the piped JSON.
entries.why: T17 (1.14): the English's hard wraps — as many lines as the English, each at most 100 characters — re-wrap, and shorten only where the words do not fit

entries.key:
"Token Pace: Disconnect Claude Status Line" restores the previous entry exactly — as long as
the entry is still the one we installed. Uninstalling the extension does not remove the entry
but deletes the script's copy with the extension's storage, and a status line still connected
would then start a script that is gone — so disconnect first if you plan to remove Token Pace.

1.14 B6 (R-RLC-113-lists, §7a Q18): a new key, the list separator — listOf applies it pairwise to every list a reader is shown (model ids, folder names, sources, paths, phrases): a, b, c = t('{0}, {1}', t('{0}, {1}', a, b), c) — write the comma your language puts between the items of a list of names and nothing more (no word for and, no bidi mark — T16 refuses a U+200F): Arabic and Persian '{0}، {1}', Chinese and Japanese '{0}、{1}' or '{0}, {1}' (your choice, named), every other language most likely '{0}, {1}' as the English — not Intl.ListFormat, which writes none in Chinese and an and before every Arabic item

1.14 B6 (R-RLC-113-lists): the same list separator on the page — the page's listOf joins its lists (the data-quality roots, the unpriced and family-priced models, the unrendered fields) through tr('{0}, {1}') — the model part's value copied, one translation in both parts

entries.key: config.showProjectNames.description
entries.why: 1.14 A1 rule 5 (§7a Q1): the default is hash now — by default a salted, stable pseudonym (safe in a screen share), with basename the name of the project's folder — and a sentence on the switch: to hash the names are dropped at once, to basename the transcripts are read again (a folder's name is read only while names are on) — translate anew

entries.key: config.attribution.description
entries.why: 1.14 A1, A2, A7: what is stored now — a salted key per project folder with the hourly figures, the folder's name only with basename, the session ids —, what a project is (a folder: its Claude Code sessions, their agents in a worktree too, a Codex session started there), and that only switching on re-reads: between project and session or back to none nothing is read again, none deletes the per-session records and the per-project split and the totals stay — the parenthesis on tool names and the Agents section word for word — translate anew
